column1: 20|Location / whereabouts|In “what’s your 20?”, the speaker is asking where you are.|Numbers|What is your 20?|I’m near the library.|what's your 20;what is your 20;what's ur 20;what is ur 20;whats your 20;your 20;ur 20;what's your twenty;what is your twenty|The number 20 alone can simply be a quantity; do not automatically treat every 20 as a location.|https://www.dictionary.com/culture/slang/whats-your-20

10-20|Location|Radio shorthand for a location, also used playfully in messages.|Numbers|What’s your 10-20?|Near the main gate.|10 20|Radio codes vary; ordinary numbers may not be slang.|https://www.dictionary.com/culture/slang/whats-your-20

10-4|Acknowledged / understood|A radio-style acknowledgment that a message was received.|Numbers|Meet at six. 10-4.|See you then.||Not a universal radio code or a substitute for confirmation in an emergency.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/10-4

67|Six seven (meme expression)|An often deliberately ambiguous meme expression; it does not have one dependable literal translation.|Numbers|Someone replies “67” as a joke.|What do you mean here?|6-7;six seven;six-seven;6 7|Often associated with Gen Alpha meme culture; a number in an ordinary sentence may just be a number.|https://www.dictionary.com/culture/slang/67

411|Information / details|In some North American informal usage, asking for “the 411” means asking for the details.|Numbers|Give me the 411 on the plan.|We’re meeting at six.|the 411|Regional and older shorthand, not a universal meaning of the number.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/411

404|Not found / missing|A web error code sometimes used jokingly for something missing or unavailable.|Numbers|Motivation: 404.|Need a break?|error 404|Its literal web meaning differs from a joke in chat. A bare 404 can be an ordinary number.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/404

1337|Elite / leet|Number-based spelling linked to leetspeak and gaming culture.|Numbers|That’s some 1337 skill.|Nicely played.|leet;l33t|Older internet wordplay; it is not a universal rating.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/1337

24/7|All the time|An idiom meaning continuously or very frequently.|Numbers|The chat is active 24/7.|It never slows down.|24-7|Often exaggeration rather than a literal claim of nonstop activity.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/24/7

101|An introduction / the basics|Used after a subject to mean its introductory principles.|Numbers|Group chat etiquette 101.|Start with the basics.||Can also be a course code or an ordinary number.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/101

rizz|Charm / charisma|Informal charm, especially when trying to attract or flirt with someone.|Social|They’ve got rizz.|They seem confident.||Having charm does not establish someone’s intentions.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rizz

no cap|No lie / honestly|An emphasis that the speaker means what they say.|Social|That was amazing, no cap.|Glad you liked it.|nocap|A sincerity marker is not proof that a statement is true.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/no_cap

cap|A lie / exaggeration|In some casual conversations, “cap” calls a claim untrue or exaggerated.|Social|That sounds like cap.|What makes you think so?||Also a hat, limit, or other ordinary word. Do not infer dishonesty from a word alone.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cap

fr|For real|An informal emphasis or question about whether someone is serious.|Chat|That happened fr?|Yes, really.|frr|Not appropriate for formal writing; context changes emphasis.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fr

frfr|For real, for real|A repeated emphasis meaning seriously or genuinely.|Chat|I need a break frfr.|Take some time.|fr fr|Can be playful or emphatic, not a guarantee of literal truth.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/frfr

ngl|Not going to lie|Introduces a candid opinion or admission.|Chat|Ngl, I’m tired.|Rest if you can.|not gonna lie|The following statement is still an opinion or claim.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/NGL
icl|I can’t lie|A casual way to introduce an honest opinion or reaction.|Chat|Icl, that was good.|Glad you enjoyed it.||Other expansions exist outside casual chat.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ICL

iykyk|If you know, you know|Signals that a reference makes sense to people who share the relevant experience.|Chat|That campus café, iykyk.|I’ve been there.|if you know you know|Can exclude people who lack context; asking for an explanation is fine.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/IYKYK

pov|Point of view|Labels a perspective; online captions may use it loosely to frame a situation.|Chat|POV: your class got cancelled.|Unexpected free time.||Online captions do not always depict an actual first-person view.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/POV

fyp|For You page|A recommendation feed label associated with TikTok and some social media discussion.|Social|It appeared on my FYP.|That algorithm knows your interests.|for you page|A tag does not guarantee reach, popularity, or recommendation placement.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/FYP

grwm|Get ready with me|A content format showing someone preparing for an activity.|Social|GRWM for university.|Have a good day.|get ready with me|Describes a format, not necessarily an invitation to meet.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/GRWM

ootd|Outfit of the day|A label for showing or describing what someone is wearing.|Social|My OOTD for the trip.|Nice outfit.|outfit of the day|Usually fashion-related; the label alone says nothing about sponsorship.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/OOTD

dm|Direct message|A private or non-public message through a platform’s messaging system.|Chat|DM me the time.|I’ll send it.|direct message;dms|Private delivery does not guarantee encryption or confidentiality.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/DM

wbu|What about you?|Asks the other person the same or a related question.|Chat|I’m studying, wbu?|Same here.|what about you|Friendly shorthand; it does not imply a relationship.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/WBU
hbu|How about you?|Returns a question to another person.|Chat|I’m okay, hbu?|Doing well, thanks.|how about you|Meaning depends on the question being returned.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/HBU
omw|On my way|The speaker says they are travelling toward a destination.|Chat|OMW to campus.|See you soon.|on my way|Does not give a reliable arrival time.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/OMW

wyd|What are you doing?|A casual question about what someone is doing.|Chat|Hey, wyd?|Working on my assignment. You?|what you doing;what are you doing|Friendly and flirtatious uses both exist; do not infer romance from this alone.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/WYD

wya|Where are you at?|A casual way to ask someone’s location.|Chat|WYA? We’re at the café.|Near the library.|where you at;where are you at|You don’t have to share your precise location.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/WYA
rn|Right now|At the present moment.|Chat|I’m busy rn.|We can talk later.|right now|Ordinary time shorthand.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/RN
lmk|Let me know|Asks someone to provide an update or answer.|Chat|LMK when you arrive.|Will do.|let me know|A request for an update, not necessarily urgency.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/LMK

smh|Shaking my head|A reaction expressing disbelief, disappointment, or disapproval.|Chat|Missed the bus again, smh.|That’s frustrating.|shaking my head|May be playful; do not assume hostility.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/SMH

istg|I swear to God|An emphatic statement that may express sincerity or frustration.|Chat|ISTG, that exam was hard.|It sounds tough.||Religious wording may not fit every audience.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ISTG
tbf|To be fair|Introduces a balancing or qualifying point.|Chat|TBF, they did warn us.|That’s a fair point.|to be fair|Other expansions exist in other domains.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/TBF

tfw|That feeling when|Introduces a situation paired with a familiar reaction.|Chat|TFW your deadline moves.|What a relief.|that feeling when|Often part of a meme caption rather than a complete sentence.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/TFW

mfw|My face when|Introduces a reaction, often with a face image or emoji.|Chat|MFW the Wi-Fi drops.|Same reaction.|my face when|A meme format; the intended expression needs context.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/MFW

irl|In real life|Refers to an offline or physical-world situation.|Chat|We finally met IRL.|How did it go?|in real life|Online relationships and experiences can still matter.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/IRL

fwiw|For what it’s worth|Introduces information or an opinion the recipient may find useful.|Chat|FWIW, the second route is faster.|Thanks, I’ll check.|for what it's worth|The value of the advice remains context-dependent.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/FWIW

iirc|If I remember correctly|Signals that the speaker is relying on uncertain memory.|Chat|IIRC, the class starts at nine.|I’ll confirm it.|if i remember correctly|A built-in uncertainty signal; verify important details.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/IIRC

icymi|In case you missed it|Introduces a reminder or previously shared information.|Chat|ICYMI, the venue changed.|Thanks for the reminder.|in case you missed it|Can sound helpful or pointed depending on context.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ICYMI

jk|Just kidding|Marks a joke or retracts a statement as playful.|Chat|I’m the best chef, jk.|That looked pretty good.|just kidding|A joke label does not make hurtful speech harmless.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/JK
np|No problem|Acknowledges thanks or reassures someone.|Chat|Thanks! NP.|Appreciate it.|no problem|Has other meanings in technical contexts.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/NP

nvm|Never mind|Withdraws a request or suggests something can be disregarded.|Chat|NVM, I found the file.|Glad you found it.|nevermind;never mind|Can sound dismissive if used without context.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/NVM

fomo|Fear of missing out|Concern about missing an experience others are having.|Social|The trip photos gave me FOMO.|We can plan another outing.|fear of missing out|Not a diagnosis or a reason to pressure someone.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/FOMO

jomo|Joy of missing out|Enjoying the choice not to participate in something.|Social|Staying home tonight: JOMO.|Enjoy your quiet evening.|joy of missing out|People can prefer different levels of social activity.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/JOMO

goat|Greatest of all time|Enthusiastic praise that someone or something is the best.|Social|That player is the GOAT.|They played brilliantly.|greatest of all time|Usually an opinion, not an objective ranking.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/GOAT

ate|Did exceptionally well|In some online praise, saying someone “ate” means they performed or looked impressive.|Social|You ate that presentation.|Thank you!|ate and left no crumbs|Also the ordinary past tense of eat; context matters.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/eat

slay|Do impressively well|An enthusiastic expression of praise or encouragement.|Social|You slayed that performance.|Thanks for cheering me on.||Also has a literal violent meaning; use context.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/slay

mid|Average / unimpressive|An informal evaluation that something is mediocre.|Social|The sequel was mid.|What didn’t work for you?||Subjective criticism, not a universal quality rating.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/mid

aura|Perceived charisma / presence|In informal online discussion, someone’s apparent confidence, coolness, or presence.|Social|That calm entrance had aura.|They seemed confident.|aura points;aura farming|“Points” are joking social evaluations, not a measurable personal worth.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/aura

brainrot|Absurd internet fixation / content|A casual label for consuming or obsessing over repetitive or absurd online content.|Social|This meme is my brainrot.|I’ve seen it everywhere.|brain rot|Not a medical diagnosis. It may refer to content or to someone’s fixation.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/brainrot

delulu|Playfully unrealistic / delusional|A humorous shortening used for unrealistic hopes or beliefs.|Social|I’m delulu about getting front-row seats.|Maybe we’ll get lucky.||Do not use it to diagnose or ridicule someone’s mental health.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/delulu

glazing|Excessive praise|In some online contexts, praising someone so much that it seems excessive.|Social|They say I’m glazing that player.|I just liked the performance.||Can be dismissive; it also has ordinary food and glass meanings.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/glaze

yap|Talk at length|An informal way to describe prolonged talking, sometimes dismissively.|Social|I could yap about that game all day.|Tell me your favorite part.|yapping;yapper|Calling someone a yapper can sound insulting.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/yap

rage bait|Content designed to provoke anger|A post or statement crafted to attract attention by upsetting people.|Social|That post looks like rage bait.|Maybe don’t engage.|ragebait|A controversial view is not automatically deliberate bait.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rage_bait

ratio|Replies or a response outweighing approval|A social-platform judgment based on reactions or a competing reply receiving more approval.|Social|The reply ratioed the original post.|People disagreed strongly.||Exact conventions vary by platform; engagement is not proof of truth.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ratio

vibe|Atmosphere / feeling|The mood or impression conveyed by a person, place, or situation.|Social|This café has a calm vibe.|It’s a good study spot.|vibes|A subjective impression, not knowledge of someone’s feelings.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/vibe

vibe check|A playful assessment of mood|A casual check of the atmosphere or someone’s apparent energy.|Social|Quick vibe check: how’s everyone?|A little tired.|vibecheck|It is not a clinical assessment or a reliable personality test.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/vibe_check

main character|Person acting as the center of attention|A playful description of someone feeling or behaving like the lead in a story.|Social|Main character moment on the walk home.|Enjoy your soundtrack.|main character energy|Can praise confidence or criticize self-centeredness depending on context.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/main_character

canon event|An apparently inevitable defining experience|A meme label for an event framed as essential to someone’s story.|Social|Missing one bus became my canon event.|That was quite a morning.||Often joking; it does not mean a harmful experience is necessary.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/canon_event

lore|Backstory / shared history|In casual online discussion, the background story behind a person, group, or situation.|Social|What’s the lore behind this photo?|It’s from our first trip.||Also has established meanings in stories, games, and tradition.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lore

side quest|An extra, unplanned activity|Borrowed from games for a secondary task or spontaneous detour.|Social|Coffee turned into a side quest.|Where did you end up?|sidequest|May be a literal game task rather than a real-world detour.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/side_quest

touch grass|Take a break from online life|An often teasing or dismissive suggestion to spend time offline.|Social|I’ve been scrolling all afternoon. Time to touch grass.|A walk sounds good.||Can insult someone; a kinder alternative is “maybe take a break.”|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/touch_grass

cooked|Exhausted / in difficulty|May mean someone is worn out, in trouble, or unlikely to succeed in a situation.|Social|I’m cooked after that exam.|How did it go?||It can also be literal cooking; ask for context rather than assuming distress.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cooked

let him cook|Give someone room to try|A playful request to let someone develop an idea or continue a performance.|Social|Wait, let him cook.|Okay, let’s hear the idea.|let them cook;let her cook|Not always approval of the outcome; it can be ironic.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/let_him_cook

lock in|Focus / commit attention|In some casual contexts, deciding to concentrate on a task.|Social|Time to lock in for finals.|Let’s study together.|locked in|Also used for literal locking or fixing an agreement.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lock_in

lowkey|Somewhat / discreetly|Can soften a statement or describe something kept understated or private.|Social|I’m lowkey nervous.|Want to talk about it?|low key|Different from highkey; the exact strength depends on context.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/low-key

highkey|Openly / strongly|A casual emphasis that something is clear, strong, or not hidden.|Social|I highkey loved that lecture.|Same here.|high key|Informal emphasis, not a literal volume or pitch.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/high-key

stan|An enthusiastic fan|A person who strongly supports an artist, creator, or other figure.|Social|I stan their music.|Which song is your favorite?||Can refer to intense fandom; respectful boundaries still matter.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/stan

ship|Want people or characters together|To support or imagine a romantic pairing.|Social|They ship those two characters.|I can see why.||Do not assume real people consent to romantic speculation.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ship

soft launch|A subtle reveal|In social posts, a hint at a relationship or announcement without a full reveal.|Social|That photo looks like a soft launch.|They might just be sharing a moment.||It can also be a business release; avoid assuming a relationship.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/soft_launch

hard launch|An explicit reveal|A direct public announcement, such as clearly introducing a relationship or project.|Social|They hard launched the new project.|Exciting news.||Meaning depends on whether the topic is social or business.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/hard_launch

green flag|A positive sign|A behavior or quality someone considers reassuring or healthy.|Social|They respect boundaries: green flag.|That matters.||One positive sign does not establish someone’s complete character.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/green_flag

red flag|A warning sign|A behavior or situation that may deserve caution or a closer look.|Social|Ignoring boundaries is a red flag.|It’s worth addressing.|redflag|Not a diagnosis or proof of wrongdoing on its own.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/red_flag

ghosting|Stopping contact without explanation|Abruptly ceasing communication with someone.|Social|They stopped replying; maybe ghosting.|That sounds frustrating.||A delayed reply alone does not establish intentional ghosting.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ghosting

situationship|An undefined romantic connection|A relationship-like connection without clear agreement about its status.|Social|We haven’t defined it; it’s a situationship.|Maybe talk about expectations.||Do not infer commitment, exclusivity, or consent.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/situationship

AFK|Away from keyboard|Temporarily absent from a game or computer.|Gaming|AFK for a minute.|See you soon.|away from keyboard|Usually temporary; not proof someone abandoned a team.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/AFK

GG|Good game|Acknowledges a match, sincerely or sometimes sarcastically.|Gaming|GG, well played.|GG!|ggwp;gg wp;good game well played|Tone can be sincere or sarcastic.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/GG

DPS|Damage per second|A game metric for damage output, also used for a damage-dealing role.|Gaming|We need more DPS.|I can switch roles.|damage per second|Game-specific calculations and role labels vary.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/DPS

NPC|Non-player character|A game character controlled by the game rather than a player.|Gaming|Talk to the NPC near the gate.|I’ll check there.|non player character;non-player character|Calling a real person an NPC can be demeaning.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/NPC

nerf|Reduce effectiveness|To weaken an ability, item, or character through a game change.|Gaming|They nerfed that weapon.|How does it feel now?||Also a brand name; this entry describes the gaming verb.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/nerf

buff|Increase effectiveness|To strengthen a game ability, item, or character, temporarily or through an update.|Gaming|The healer got a buff.|Nice, let’s test it.||Game meanings vary; also an ordinary word outside games.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/buff

clutch|Succeed under pressure|To make a crucial successful play in a difficult moment.|Gaming|You clutched the last round.|Team effort!||Also has non-gaming meanings.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/clutch

POG|An excited reaction|An expression of excitement or appreciation associated with streaming culture.|Gaming|That comeback was POG.|What a play.|poggers|Community-specific; not everyone recognizes it.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pog

EOD|End of day|A loose work deadline near the end of a day.|Work|Send the draft by EOD.|Which time and time zone?|end of day|Confirm the exact deadline and time zone.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/EOD

OOO|Out of office|Away from regular work availability.|Work|I’m OOO tomorrow.|Thanks for the heads-up.|out of office|Does not establish someone’s precise availability.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/OOO
WFH|Work from home|Working remotely from home.|Work|WFH today.|See you on the call.|work from home|Not necessarily a day off or constant availability.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/WFH

ASAP|As soon as possible|A request to act at the earliest practical time.|Work|Can you review ASAP?|What deadline should I prioritize?|as soon as possible|It is better to specify a real deadline.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ASAP

TL;DR|Too long; didn’t read / short summary|May introduce a concise summary or dismiss a long message.|Chat|TL;DR: meet at six.|Got it.|tldr;tl dr|Can sound dismissive when directed at someone’s message.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/TL;DR

kya scene hai|What’s the plan / situation?|A casual Roman Urdu question about plans or what is happening.|Regional|Aaj kya scene hai?|Library chalte hain.|kia scene hai;kya scene;kiya scene hai|Not just a literal scene; tone and relationship matter.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/scene

scene on hai|The plan is happening|A casual Pakistani English/Roman Urdu confirmation that a plan is active.|Regional|Kal coffee? Scene on hai.|Done, milte hain.|scene on|Local informal usage; not every speaker uses it the same way.|

chalo|Let’s go / okay then|A Roman Urdu/Hindi expression used to move a plan forward or acknowledge something.|Regional|Chalo, class ke liye chalte hain.|Chalo.|chalo phir|Can express a suggestion, acceptance, or resignation.|

acha|Okay / really / good|A Roman Urdu acknowledgment or reaction with several context-dependent uses.|Regional|Acha, phir milte hain.|Theek hai.|achha;accha;achaa|Tone changes whether it sounds surprised, approving, or neutral.|
haan|Yes|An affirmative response in Roman Urdu/Hindi.|Regional|Haan, main aa raha hoon.|Theek hai.|han;haan ji|Regional spellings vary; it may be an acknowledgment rather than full agreement.|
nahi|No / not|A negative response or negation in Roman Urdu/Hindi.|Regional|Nahi, aaj class nahi hai.|Acha, thanks.|nai;nahin;nehin|Mixed-language context matters.|
bas|Enough / just|A short word used for a limit, amount, or emphasis in Roman Urdu/Hindi.|Regional|Bas, itna kaafi hai.|Theek hai.||Also used in other languages with different meanings.|

jugaad|An improvised workaround|A resourceful workaround or makeshift solution in South Asian usage.|Regional|Is ka koi jugaad hai?|Let’s find a proper fix.|jugaar|A workaround is not always safe or reliable.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/jugaad

1437|I love you forever|A number code based on the letter counts in “I / love / you / forever”.|Numbers|1437 ❤️|That’s sweet.||A possible affectionate code, not a universal meaning of an ordinary number.|https://www.cyberdefinitions.com/text_speak_based_on_numbers.html

831|I love you|One code reads as eight letters, three words, one meaning: “I love you”.|Numbers|They sent “831”.|What does that mean for you?||Numeric codes need shared context; do not assume a relationship.|https://www.cyberdefinitions.com/text_speak_based_on_numbers.html

520|I love you (Chinese numeric code)|In Chinese messaging, 520 can represent a sound-based “I love you” code.|Numbers|520 ❤️|That’s kind of you.||Language and relationship context matter; a bare number may just be a number.|https://www.cyberdefinitions.com/text_speak_based_on_numbers.html

1314|For a lifetime / forever (Chinese code)|In Chinese numeric wordplay, this can suggest a lifetime or lasting commitment.|Numbers|They paired 520 with 1314.|Could you explain the code?||Not a universal code or proof of someone’s intentions.|https://www.slang.org/1314-meaning-definition/

5201314|I love you for a lifetime|Combines two Chinese sound-based numeric codes into an affectionate expression.|Numbers|They wrote “5201314”.|That’s a thoughtful message.||Interpret only within a shared language and relationship context.|https://www.cyberdefinitions.com/text_speak_based_on_numbers.html

555|Laughter in Thai; other uses vary|In Thai online chat, fives can imitate “ha ha ha”. Some Chinese contexts instead use repeated fives for crying.|Numbers|That joke was funny 555.|Glad it made you laugh.|5555;55555;555+;๕๕๕|The language can reverse the interpretation. Do not label it universally as either laughter or crying.|https://slang.net/meaning/555

88|Bye-bye in some Chinese chats|A sound-based goodbye used in some Chinese-language online messaging.|Numbers|Talk tomorrow, 88.|Bye!||Has other meanings in other communities and can simply be the number 88. Do not infer an ideology or intent from the number alone.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/88

420|Cannabis-culture reference|A number associated with cannabis culture in some contexts.|Numbers||||An explanatory reference, not an invitation to use substances. Ordinary quantities, dates, and times may be literal.|https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/420
